record.original_question: Consider the one-dimensional heavy-ball setting on F_{mu,L}, and let the purple region denote the set of tunings (gamma, beta) for which there exists a function in F_{mu,L} and an initialization whose heavy-ball trajectory forms a cycle. Can one prove that, in dimension 1, this full purple region of cycling tunings is actually achieved, thereby proving that heavy-ball cannot accelerate in dimension 1 either?

evidence.quote: While this numerical observation does not constitute a mathematical proof, this leads us to believe that HB cannot accelerate, even in dimension 1.

Ultimately, we therefore have two connected conjectures: (i) Can we prove that the purple region representing all the cycles, is achieved in dimension 1, therefore proving that HB cannot accelerate in dimension 1 either?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $0 < \mu \le L < \infty$ and let $\mathcal{F}_{\mu,L}$ denote the class of continuously differentiable functions $f:\mathbb{R}\to\mathbb{R}$ that are $\mu$-strongly convex and $L$-smooth (i.e., $\nabla f$ is $L$-Lipschitz and $f - \tfrac{\mu}{2}\|\cdot\|^2$ is convex). The Heavy-Ball (HB) iteration with step-size $\gamma>0$ and momentum $\beta\in\mathbb{R}$ is
$$x_{k+1} = x_k - \gamma f'(x_k) + \beta(x_k - x_{k-1}), \qquad k\ge 1,$$
with given $x_0,x_1\in\mathbb{R}$. Call a trajectory $(x_k)_{k\ge 0}$ a cycle if there exist integers $p\ge 1$ and $k_0\ge 0$ such that $x_{k+p}=x_k$ for all $k\ge k_0$, and the trajectory is not eventually constant at the minimizer of $f$.

Define the cycling region
$$\mathcal{C} = \{(\gamma,\beta)\in\mathbb{R}_{>0}\times\mathbb{R} : \exists\, f\in\mathcal{F}_{\mu,L},\ \exists\, (x_0,x_1)\in\mathbb{R}^2 \text{ such that the HB trajectory is a cycle}\}.$$

Numerical exploration suggests an explicit ("purple") region $\mathcal{P}\subseteq \mathbb{R}_{>0}\times\mathbb{R}$ of tunings for which cycles seemingly arise in dimension one. 

Prove that $\mathcal{C}=\mathcal{P}$, i.e., the entire conjectured cycling region is actually realized by some function in $\mathcal{F}_{\mu,L}$ and some initialization in dimension one. As a consequence, deduce that the Heavy-Ball method admits no worst-case asymptotic acceleration over $\mathcal{F}_{\mu,L}$ in dimension one: there is no choice of $(\gamma,\beta)$ achieving a contraction rate strictly better than that of gradient descent uniformly over $\mathcal{F}_{\mu,L}$.
artifact.status_search_result: The problem is posed as an explicit open problem in a 2025 preprint titled "Open Problem: Two Riddles in Heavy-Ball Dynamics" by Goujaud, Taylor, and Dieuleveut. A related companion paper (Mathematical Programming, 2025) proves non-acceleration results for Heavy-Ball but leaves the full dimension-1 cycling-region question unresolved. No subsequent work resolving the conjecture was found.

status_evidence.title: Open Problem: Two Riddles in Heavy-Ball Dynamics
status_evidence.snippet: presents two open problems on Polyak's Heavy-Ball algorithm... ability to exactly accelerate in dimension one
status_evidence.claim: The dimension-1 cycling/non-acceleration question is explicitly stated as an open problem.

status_evidence.title: Provable non-accelerations of the heavy-ball method
status_evidence.snippet: Provable non-accelerations of the heavy-ball method, Mathematical Programming 2025
status_evidence.claim: Related non-acceleration results have been established, but not the full dimension-1 cycling region conjecture.
